NextItNet implementations use causal convolutions with left padding `(kernel_size−1)×dilation` and normalization across channels at each timestep. On `[B,L,C]`, use `LayerNorm(C)`; including time in normalization can leak future information. Sources: [NextItNet implementation](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html), [PyTorch LayerNorm](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/normalization.py). Implementation implication: retain the original token mask `m=(sequence!=0)[...,None]`, zero padded embeddings, and reapply it after each convolution→LayerNorm→activation/dropout stage, before the next temporal convolution. Also mask residual sums and final normalization outputs. Convolution biases and LayerNorm’s learned offset can recreate nonzero padded states; masking only embeddings or block outputs lets those states contaminate real-token features inside a block. For pre-normalized blocks, mask after normalization before temporal mixing.

Recommended regression tests, with dropout disabled: (1) change or append future tokens after every tested cutoff; all features and scores through that cutoff must remain equal within numerical tolerance. Optionally verify zero gradients from an output at time t to input embeddings after t. (2) Compare a history with the same history preceded by several different numbers of PAD tokens, without truncation; aligned real-token features and candidate scores must agree. Read the final nonpadding position, never `count−1` for left-padded sequences. Exercise short histories, every dilation, multiple blocks, mixed-length batches, and deliberately nonzero convolution biases/LayerNorm offsets so initialization cannot hide failures. Check intermediate padded activations remain zero and repeat after training and checkpoint reload. These tests establish empirical causality and padding invariance separately; neither property alone establishes the other.
